title: Invitation Background Pattern — the printed invitation's pattern on the site
problem_statement: The site's Theme tokens were sampled from the wedding invitation's fig-and-foliage artwork, but the pattern itself — the most recognizable part of the invitation Guests hold in their hands — appears nowhere on the site. The site reads as color-coordinated with the invitation rather than as one piece with it.
solution: Bring the invitation pattern onto the site the way the printed invitation itself uses it: pattern in the margins and text-free zones, content in a clean cream window, readability never traded for decoration. The candidate treatment layers a muted forest/sage duotone derivative of the pattern as the page wall (content floats on cream panels) with full-color fig and Golden Gate motifs as accents in text-free zones — the accents are what keep the pattern present on phones, where full-width content covers the wall. Because this is a design-direction call, the treatment is prototyped on the Home Page first; the Team Lead reviews it on his phone and rules on the direction before any site-wide rollout.

user_stories.want: the site to look and feel like the invitation I received
user_stories.benefit: the wedding's identity is one continuous piece from paper to screen

user_stories.want: text that stays perfectly legible everywhere
user_stories.benefit: the decoration never gets in the way of the details I came for

user_stories.want: to see the pattern treatment live on my phone before committing the whole site to it
user_stories.benefit: I make the design-direction call on evidence, not mockups

implementation_decisions.title: The supplied seamless tile is the pattern source of record
implementation_decisions.summary: The Team Lead supplied the invitation pattern as a square seamless tile (source material, alongside the invitation proof). Measured near-seamless: the top/bottom wrap is clean; the left/right wrap shows a faint seam. Acceptance is no visible seam at the final display treatment; minor seam-blending on the derived assets is the fallback.

implementation_decisions.title: Derived assets, not the raw art, go behind content
implementation_decisions.summary: An asset-derivation step produces (a) a muted single-color forest/sage duotone tile at near-watermark contrast for the page wall, and (b) optimized full-color motif assets for text-free accent zones (hero band, section dividers, corner ornaments). The full-color pattern never sits under body text; text contrast is always measured against the solid cream panel, never the tile.

implementation_decisions.title: Prototype on Home, then the ruling gate
implementation_decisions.summary: The layered treatment (muted wall + color accents) is built on the Home Page only, on a preview deployment. The Team Lead reviews on mobile and desktop and rules: layered as-is, wall-only, accents-only, or drop. No other Page changes until the ruling lands.

implementation_decisions.title: Site-wide rollout is a separate, gated body of work
implementation_decisions.summary: After the ruling, the chosen treatment extends to the remaining Pages (including the Name gate screen and any lightbox-free zones judged text-free). The rollout inherits the ruling verbatim — no per-page reinterpretation.

implementation_decisions.title: Pattern assets ride the Theme, honoring tokens-only styling
implementation_decisions.summary: Pattern layers consume Theme tokens for any color they carry (duotone recolor targets the token palette) and degrade gracefully: no pattern behind text at any viewport, static fallback where motion-adjacent effects would appear, and prefers-reduced-motion respected. Whether the pattern asset reference itself becomes a theme-level token is an implementation call for the architect within the tokens-only philosophy.

testing_decisions: No automated tests per the Team Lead's selection — the feature is visual. Quality is gated by the mandatory UI-change sequence (design-reviewer → process-adherence), the token-style adherence check, and the Team Lead's prototype ruling.
WCAG contrast of text against its cream panel is re-verified as part of design review on every Page the treatment touches.
out_of_scope: Full-color pattern tiled directly behind body text — rejected on legibility principle.
Fixed/parallax edge-reveal effects — desktop-only benefit, motion-accessibility cost, mobile-heavy audience.
Redrawing or reinterpreting the invitation motifs as new artwork — the supplied tile is the source.
Any change to the palette or fonts — Theme tokens stay as-is; this PRD adds pattern, not color.
Site-wide rollout ahead of the Team Lead's prototype ruling.
notes: Provenance: Epic Grill session 2026-07-07 (.excn/gallery-pattern-grill_progress.json); treatment direction informed by a commissioned research digest on tasteful pattern usage (Morris/toile principles, Che Fico's own fig-motif branding, mobile degradation idioms).
The prototype ruling is the PRD's central open decision; issue breakdown should make the ruling an explicit gate between the prototype slice and every rollout slice.
